comment.undefined: The status of the award: a movie can win a specific awards, or just be nominated for it
A project (a collective endeavour of some kind).
A personal profile RDF document.
An actor or actress who acted in the movie
A scale based on five starts, with one star being a low rating and five being the highest.
A movie, identified by its title, date of release and people involved in its realization. It's assigned one or more ratings and can be awarded or nominated for one or more awards.
An online account.
The entity giving a rating, consisting either of a group of voters or of a single voter.
The screenwriter of a movie. A movie can have more than one screenwriter.
An image.
The producer of a movie. A movie can have more than one producer.
An agent (eg. person, group, software or physical artifact).
An organization.
The main language spoken in the movie.
A ten-based scale, with 1 being the lowest score and 10 the highest.
The rating given to a movie, consisting of a score (numerical, string, etc) expressed according to a scale (percentage, stars) and issued by a rating body.
A person.
The genre of a movie, i.e. adventure, or rom-com. A movie can have multiple genres.
A percentage-based scale, with lower percentages representing scarce appreciation.
An online chat account.
An online gaming account.
A foaf:LabelProperty is any RDF property with texual values that serve as labels.
The director of a movie. A movie can have one or more directors.
An organization or event assigning awards to movies and people involved in their productions
An award given by an awarding body to a movie or a person involved in its production
The scale defining the score, i.e., percentages, 1 to 5 stars, 1-10 scale.
A group of people expressing a rating.
An online e-commerce account.
A document.
A class of Agents.
The category of the award, i.e. "Best Cinematography" of the BSFC Award.
Property expressing the value, numerical or literal, of a rating.
A work info homepage of some person; a page about their work for some organization.
The original title of a movie.
Property relating the movie with the awards.
Property relating the rating authority to the rating it expressed. Inverse of "expressedBy".
A location that something is based near, for some broadly human notion of near.
A page or document about this thing.
The property connects the rating with its source, e.g, "IMDb".
The given name of some person.
A checksum for the DNA of some thing. Joke.
A Yahoo chat ID
A name for some thing.
An ICQ chat ID
The given name of some person.
The name of an award's category, e.g. "Top Box Office Movie".
A document that this thing is the primary topic of.
Property declaring the main title a movie is known with.
A depiction of some thing.
The family name of some person.
Property connecting the movie with its producer. Inverse of "produced".
Title (Mr, Mrs, Ms, Dr. etc)
Indicates an account held by this agent.
A tipjar document for this agent, describing means for payment and reward.
Property specifying the main language spoken in a movie.
Property connecting two people who have worked on the same movie, regardless of their specific job.
An AIM chat ID
A Skype ID
Property connecting a movie to its screenwriter. Inverse of "wrote".
A topic of some page or document.
An image that can be used to represent some thing (ie. those depictions which are particularly representative of something, eg. one's photo on a homepage).
A sha1sum hash, in hex.
The property connects a rating with the movie it describes. Inverse of "hasRating".
The first name of a person.
Something that was made by this agent.
The property specifies the type of genre of a movie.
The director who directed the movie. Inverse of "directedBy".
The property connects the movie with the actor/actress who acted in it. Inverse of "actedIn".
The family name of some person.
Property connecting the award to the awarding body or event that assigns it. Inverse of "gives".
A .plan comment, in the tradition of finger and '.plan' files.
The number of votes that determine the score, i.e., a five-star score based on twenty votes.
A Myers Briggs (MBTI) personality classification.
Property specifying the name of a deciding body (assigning an award or a rating).
A link to the publications of this person.
A page about a topic of interest to this person.

comment.undefined: The sha1sum of the URI of an Internet mailbox associated with exactly one owner, the  first owner of the mailbox.
Property relating the movie with its director(s). Inverse of "directed".
A short informal nickname characterising an agent (includes login identifiers, IRC and other chat nicknames).
Property specifying the category of the award related to a movie, e.g. "Top Box Office Movie".
The property specifying whether a movie was only nominated or also won an award.
An OpenID for an Agent.
A project this person has previously worked on.
The person producing a movie. Inverse of "producedBy".
A theme.
A person known by this person (indicating some level of reciprocated interaction between the parties).
The underlying or 'focal' entity associated with some SKOS-described concept.
A phone,  specified using fully qualified tel: URI scheme (refs: http://www.w3.org/Addressing/schemes.html#tel).
A thing depicted in this representation.
A textual geekcode for this person, see http://www.geekcode.com/geek.html
The primary topic of some page or document.
A homepage of a school attended by the person.
The gender of this Agent (typically but not necessarily 'male' or 'female').
The last name of a person.
The property relates the rating body with the people constituting it.
A string expressing what the user is happy for the general public (normally) to know about their current activity.
The property connecting a score to the scale used to express it.
Property declaring the main title a movie is known with.

Indicates a homepage of the service provide for this online account.
A logo representing some thing.
An organization funding a project or person.

Indicates the name (identifier) associated with this online account.
Any activity perfomed by a person while working on a movie, i.e., producing, writing, taking care of photography or costumes.
A jabber ID for something.
The age in years of some agent.
A homepage for some thing.

A thing of interest to this person.
A current project this person works on.
Indicates an account held by this agent.
A derived thumbnail image.
A weblog of some thing (whether person, group, company etc.).
The birthday of this Agent, represented in mm-dd string form, eg. '12-31'.
The name of an award's category, e.g. "Top Box Office Movie".
The property specifies the type of genre of a movie.
Indicates a member of a Group

A  personal mailbox, ie. an Internet mailbox associated with exactly one owner, the first owner of this mailbox. This is a 'static inverse functional property', in that  there is (across time and change) at most one individual that ever has any particular value for foaf:mbox.
The surname of some person.
An agent that  made this thing.
Property relating the movie to its genres.
Property specifying the date of release of a movie, expressed only by its year, e.g. "2015".
